Post Title: "Strategy" is the most misunderstood term amongst SaaS founders.
Body:
After 5+ years in B2B SaaS, I am 100% convinced that word "Strategy" is the most misunderstood term amongst SaaS founders.
Why I say so?

Because when marketing strategy is discussed,
this is what I hear most:

- run campaigns
- activate new channels
- product demos
- launches
- webinars
- demand gen

.....the list can go on.

But all these, in principal, are "tactics".

The foundations on which these run is "Strategy".

Let's take a short dive into business literature 👇

To double check how "Strategy" is defined,
(and flex my B-school degree 😅, kidding!)

I literally pulled out my textbook on the course "Strategy".
And here's what it said:

[Strategy is a deliberate set of choices that positions an organization to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage and superior long-term performance relative to its competitors]

----------------------------

Then I went a step further to find how marketing gurus explain the term "Strategy".

> Roger L. Martin (In his book "Playing to Win")
"Strategy is an integrated cascade of choices that tells you what game you're playing, where you will play it, and how you will win."

> Seth Godin
"It's a philosophy of becoming. I don't think it's a set of tactics. I don't think it's about winning in the short run. I think it's about being very clear about the change we seek to make and who we seek to change."

> Michael Porter
"Operational effectiveness is not strategy."

Did you notice the common thread?

Choices.
Positioning.
Where to play.
Who to change.

----------------------------

So, in the most fundamental sense,

Strategy is:

- positioning you want to take in the market
- to decide which category you want to compete in
- to decide for whom you are
- to decide for whom you are not
- to decide which channels to go after

How to execute it is when campaigns, activating channels, launches, etc. come into picture.

====================

If you are a SaaS founder reading this,
and is trapped in "tactics" disguised as "strategy".

It's time you take action.

I can help you build one.
DM.

Post Title: 6 months ago, I moved from Bengaluru to Pune.
Body:
6 months ago, I moved from Bengaluru to Pune.
And for someone who work with SaaS founders for living, that's a big shift. Because...

...in Bengaluru, walk into any café, pin point a person,
50% chances they are a SaaS founder (my ICP)

(okay, may be a bit of an exaggeration, but you get the idea)

What I miss most about Bengaluru?

→ Cafe Culture
Amazing coffee, work-friendly spots, full of people building, hustling, debating the next big idea.

→ Food
IMO, no city in India beats Bengaluru on variety, global cuisines, and authenticity. Dosa (or Dosae) is something to die for.

→ Lakes & Gardens
As someone into fitness, a walk/run on a track surrounding a lake is true heaven. Needless to mention a day well spent in cubbon park.

→ Conversations
Startups, fundings, VCs, the latest thing someone built an app for. Usual talking points with colleagues, at networking events.

→ Weather
Mayyybe. Pune has decent weather too. Infact, one of the reasons I picked this city.

→ Traffic
Haha...let's not talk about it. Pune's traffic is a breeze to someone who spent time in Bengaluru.

---------------------------------------

Anyways, now I am settled in here.
The city is slowly growing over me and I am kinda loving it here too.

I have figured out some great cafés to work from.
Found a few food spots I keep going back to.

But the one thing I am still building is the network.
A network of fellow marketers, PMMs, and SaaS founders.

So if you are reading this -

DM, if you are a startup or SaaS marketer. Let's discuss PMM-life, startup world, and trade notes.

Happy Monday! 😊

Post Title: I'm 32. Married. Left 9-5. Now self employed.
Body:
I'm 32. Married. Left 9-5. Now self employed.
And I no more spend my week like before…

when I was working full-time.

How it's like now?

- working 10+ hours a day
- reading more books now
- hitting gym more regularly
- high on energy every morning
- questioning my decision by noon
- re-regulating my thoughts by evening
- disturbing my wife couple of times, because I wfh
- receiving kind words from old acquaintances
- getting to know a lot of new people
- working on weekends sometimes
- brewing my own coffee 2x a day
- churning more and more ideas

So, yes I no more spend the week like before.

But, I love the way I am spending it now.
Working on building something, inch by inch.

Yes, it's full of uncertainties but fun!
